content: 1. High-risk behaviors do not pose a risk of person-to-person transmission through casual contact. For example, the perception that a village was selected due to being problematic is incorrect. 2. If a cluster survey is used, the team will explain to the population that the selection is based on households rather than individuals. Within each selected household, all individuals will be invited to participate. 3. Care will be taken to ensure that the explanation of random selection is communicated in a culturally and educationally appropriate manner. 4. A full report of the survey results will be shared with decision-makers. Shorter reports will be sent to participating primary care facilities, and a scientific article will be submitted to a peer-reviewed journal. 5. Further use of the data is detailed in Section XIII, which outlines the expected benefits of the survey. The results will not be shared at the cluster level, as this would lack statistical meaning and could increase the risk of stigmatization. 6. Given the low prevalence of hepatitis, the number of individuals testing positive in each cluster is expected to be limited. This will facilitate confidential follow-up for those testing positive, reducing the risk of stigmatization. 7. Field workers will be trained to minimize any negative consequences of blood collection. They will use sterile, single-use equipment and adhere to WHO best practices for blood collection. 8. Participants may experience minor discomfort, such as bleeding, bruising, or swelling at the blood draw site. Rarely, fainting or infection may occur. 9. The questionnaire will be administered privately in the participant's home. Confidentiality will be maintained using unique identifier codes on questionnaires and databases. Names will not be written on the questionnaire headers or entered into any computer system. 10. The same identifier code will be used on laboratory specimens, questionnaires, and consent forms, utilizing pre-printed stickers or barcodes. 11. To ensure the return of results to individuals, full identifying data will be written on consent forms, which will be securely stored under the principal investigator's responsibility. These forms will be destroyed or handled according to data protection regulations after the study is completed and results are returned. 12. Investigators will ensure that participants can access their test results within a reasonable timeframe. If rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs) are used, results will be provided immediately in a confidential manner, along with adequate post-test counseling. 13. For laboratory-based in vitro diagnosis, results will be available after a few weeks. Participants will be able to call a designated number to access their results using their identifier code. 14. Individuals testing positive will be actively followed up by investigators to arrange referrals for care and treatment assessment. 15. Upon arrival at a household, trained field enumerators will introduce themselves and the authority on whose behalf they are conducting the study. 16. Participants (or their parents) will be fully informed about the risks and benefits of participation. They will sign a written informed consent form or document their consent through other means if illiterate or underage (assent). 17. If a participant cannot read, a relative from the same household may serve as a witness and sign on their behalf. 18. In cluster sampling, upon arrival at a pre-selected household, the surveyor will invite all eligible household members to participate. Consent will be obtained from eligible individuals (or their parents or household head). 19. If more than one person in the household needs to provide consent, the informed consent information will be read to all individuals simultaneously, with an opportunity to ask questions. 20. One person may provide consent for themselves and their children. They will be asked to provide consent individually for themselves and their children. 21. Children will be read an information sheet in simplified language and asked to sign a dedicated assent form for the questionnaire and blood collection. Children under six years of age will not be asked to assent due to their inability to understand the procedure. 22. During the consent process, participants will be asked if they agree to the storage of their blood specimens for future testing deemed relevant by the Ministry of Health. This is optional. 23. Specimens will be anonymized at the end of the study, breaking the link between the patient and the unique identifier. Results of any future testing will not be returned to the participant. 24. Patients identified with HBV or HCV infection during the biomarker survey will be referred for care. 25. If a statistical sample is used, the survey will generate reliable, population-based estimates of the prevalence of viral hepatitis biomarkers. 26. These estimates will provide information about the country's status in achieving regional and global control or elimination goals. 27. The estimates will also serve as input parameters for modeling work to estimate the current burden of infection and evaluate prevention, testing, and treatment options, such as vaccination, infection control, and care. 28. All participating institutions will be listed along with their roles and responsibilities, including contact information for key personnel. 29. A written report of the survey will be prepared within four months of completing testing. Investigators will organize a debriefing session with stakeholders to ensure the information is utilized. 30. The principal investigator will prepare a manuscript for submission to a peer-reviewed journal. Authorship will be determined based on international criteria and contributions. 31. All procedures associated with the biomarker survey will be planned according to a timeline, including reserving sessions with the ethics committee in advance. 32. The budget will follow the estimate provided in the template budget for a hepatitis biomarker survey. 33. Data collected from the survey will only be accessible to the implementing institution and its partners, who will maintain strict confidentiality. 34. Participants' names will not appear on any survey records or computer systems. Instead, a unique number will be used to ensure anonymity. 35. When presenting or publishing survey results, no reference will be made to participants' names. The key to the code will be securely stored.
